title: How Breathing Works
keyIdea: Air goes in through the nose or mouth, down the windpipe, into the lungs. Lungs take oxygen the body needs. We breathe out carbon dioxide waste. The chest rises on breathe-in and falls on breathe-out.

kid: When you breathe in, air goes through your nose or mouth, down your windpipe, into your lungs.
Your lungs take oxygen from the air. Your body needs oxygen to stay alive.
When you breathe out, you send out carbon dioxide. That is waste gas.
Feel your chest: it rises when you breathe in and falls when you breathe out.
adult: Ages 5–7 human body: nose/mouth → windpipe → lungs; oxygen in, carbon dioxide out; chest movement. KS1 animals including humans — basic needs include air. Words: windpipe, lungs, oxygen, carbon dioxide.
Common mistakes: thinking we breathe out oxygen; thinking air stops at the mouth; mixing the windpipe with the food tube; ignoring chest movement.
In the lab your child builds the air path, chooses oxygen in and carbon dioxide out, moves the chest in and out, matches gas jobs, and ticks the full breath story.

familyTip: Put a hand on the ribs and take three slow breaths together. Ask 'what is going in?' and 'what is going out?'
